% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{abstract}
Six-bar tensegrity rovers roll by deforming their cable network, but
their gaits are developed in simulators that can inject energy, and
their suspended payloads are rarely examined. We present three
cable-only controllers on an energy-audited simulator. Sensitivity-Gradient
Tipping (SGT) differentiates the pinned quasi-static equilibrium and
reaches \nSgtSpeed\,m/s, where support-face LQR, iLQR and MPC schedulers
advance at most \baseBestProgress\,m in 20\,s. MPC + GPS, an MPC-guided
policy search whose teacher reduces exactly to SGT, learns a cable
policy reaching \gpsRatio\,\% of SGT's progress on held-out conditions.
A suspension-integrity filter with discrete-time barrier conditions
reduces payload-cable slack from \shSlackOffSgt\,\% to \shSlackOnSgt\,\%
of the time and increases SGT's progress by \shProgGainSgt\,\%. Code:
\coderepo.
\end{abstract}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Introduction}

Six-bar spherical tensegrities combine low mass with high impact
tolerance and have been studied as planetary landers and rovers
\cite{sabelhaus2015superball,littlefield2019kinodynamic}. They move by
\emph{punctuated rolling}: changing cable rest lengths deforms the shell
until the centre of mass (COM) leaves the triangular support face and
the structure tips onto a neighbouring face (Fig.~\ref{fig:teaser}).
Because hardware is expensive and fragile, gaits are developed in
simulation \cite{mirletz2015reality,zhang2017deep} and transferred
later, which makes two questions central: does the simulated motion come
from the cables, and does the gait leave the payload it carries intact?

General engines such as MuJoCo and Bullet
\cite{todorov2012mujoco,coumans2015bullet} and dedicated tensegrity
simulators \cite{mirletz2015reality} treat bars as rigid bodies or stiff
penalty springs whose drift is removed by stabilization
\cite{baumgarte1972} or by position projection (SHAKE/RATTLE
\cite{ryckaert1977shake,andersen1983rattle}); contacts are often
clamped, and interactive simulators add ``assist'' torques so that a
gait looks convincing. Each of these changes the mechanical energy
without a physical work term, and structure-preserving integrators
\cite{hairer2006geometric} do not by themselves expose such sources.
On the control side, rolling gaits have been obtained from hand-designed
cable sequences, kinodynamic planning over gait primitives
\cite{littlefield2019kinodynamic} and reinforcement learning, including
guided policy search on SUPERball \cite{zhang2017deep}. Guided policy
search trains a policy by supervised learning on local trajectory
optimizers that are kept close to it \cite{levine2013guided,
montgomery2016mdgps}; its MPC-guided variant uses a model-predictive
teacher \cite{zhang2016mpcgps}, and PLATO and DAgger train on the
learner's own state distribution \cite{kahn2017plato,ross2011dagger}.
Control barrier functions enforce safety by a minimal correction of a
nominal input \cite{ames2017cbf,agrawal2017dcbf}, but we are not aware
of their use for the suspension of a tensegrity payload. Classic
support-face gaits, finally, contract a fixed cable set; with a
realistic stroke and a heavy payload such a primitive may not move the
COM far enough to tip, however its effort is scheduled.

Building on an \emph{energy-audited} simulator---a non-minimal
Lagrangian model \cite{nonminimal_preprint} with exact bar multipliers,
passive contact and a work ledger that measures, before correction, the
energy that each step creates without a booked cause---we make three
contributions (Fig.~\ref{fig:arch}): (1) \emph{Sensitivity-Gradient
Tipping} (SGT), a cable-only gait that differentiates the pinned
quasi-static equilibrium of shell and payload, including the geometric
stiffness of the compressed bars, and drives the COM across a support
edge; (2) \emph{MPC + GPS}, an MPC-guided policy search---throughout,
GPS denotes Guided Policy Search---whose receding-horizon QP teacher on
the SGT sensitivity reduces exactly to SGT in a limit and trains a
permutation-equivariant per-cable policy; and (3) the observation that
the payload suspension of a rolling six-bar rover loses its pretension,
with a \emph{suspension-integrity filter} that minimally corrects any
tipping controller using the same sensitivities. All methods are
evaluated on a seed-locked protocol (114 runs for SGT and five
baselines, 24 for policy training and evaluation, 40 for the filter),
and every number in the text is generated from the run files. All
claims are restricted to simulation, and the negative results for the
baselines concern the support-face primitive they schedule, not the
optimal-control methods as such.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Energy-Audited Shell Dynamics}\label{sec:model}

\subsection{Coordinates, Mass and Constraints}
The shell has $n=12$ nodes $\vect q\in\R^{36}$, six bars connecting node
pairs $(i,j)$ and 24 outer cables; the payload core is a point mass
$m_c$ suspended by 12 cables. Bar $k$ of length $l_k$, mass $m_k$ and
radius $r_k$ is a uniform cylinder, which gives the consistent block
mass matrix (times $I_3$)
\begin{equation}
\vect M_k=\begin{bmatrix} a_k+m_i & b_k\\ b_k & a_k+m_j\end{bmatrix},\;
a_k=\tfrac{m_k}{4}+\tfrac{J_k}{l_k^2},\;
b_k=\tfrac{m_k}{4}-\tfrac{J_k}{l_k^2},
\end{equation}
with $J_k=\tfrac{m_k}{12}(3r_k^2+l_k^2)$ and node masses $m_i$. The bars
are node-disjoint, so $\vect M$ is block diagonal with closed-form
inverse. The bar constraints are $R_k(\vect q)=\|\vect b_k\|^2-l_k^2=0$,
$\vect b_k=\vect q_j-\vect q_i$, with Jacobian $\vect R_q$.

\subsection{Equations of Motion and Correction}
With $\vect F$ collecting gravity, cable, damping, contact and payload
forces, the index-1 form of $\vect M\ddot{\vect q}=\vect F+\vect R_q^\top\vect\lambda$
gives the multipliers in closed form,
\begin{equation}
\vect\lambda=-\big(\vect R_q\vect M^{-1}\vect R_q^\top\big)^{-1}
\big(\vect\xi_2+\vect R_q\vect M^{-1}\vect F\big),\quad
\xi_{2,k}=2\|\dot{\vect b}_k\|^2,
\label{eq:lambda}
\end{equation}
and the bar compression $P_k=2\lambda_k l_k$ ($\Delta t=2$\,ms,
semi-implicit Euler). After every step the minimum-norm corrector of
\cite{nonminimal_preprint} iterates, for at most ten iterations,
\begin{subequations}\label{eq:corr}
\begin{align}
\vect r&=\big[\vect R;\ \dot{\vect R};\ E+V_c-(E^\star+\delta W)\big],\\
\vect d&=-\vect A^\top(\vect A\vect A^\top)^{-1}\vect r,\quad
\vect A=\partial\vect r/\partial[\vect q;\dot{\vect q};\delta W],\\
[\vect q;\dot{\vect q};\delta W]&\leftarrow[\vect q;\dot{\vect q};\delta W]+\vect d,
\end{align}
\end{subequations}
where $E^\star$ is the energy predicted by the work ledger and the
correction work $\delta W$ is booked explicitly instead of being hidden.
Our extension is the contact potential $V_c$ in the energy function. The
energy row is enforced only while $|E-E^\star|\le\max(0.5\,\mathrm{J},0.02|E|)$,
so a gross modelling error is reported rather than corrected.

\subsection{Passive Contact}
For penetration $p=\max(0,h(x,y)-z)$ into terrain $h$, the normal force
is the Hunt--Crossley law \cite{hunt1975coefficient}
$\vect f_n=k\,p^{3/2}(1+\alpha\dot p)\hat{\vect n}$, whose elastic part
has potential $V_c=\tfrac{2}{5}k\,p^{5/2}$ and whose damping only
dissipates; friction is a regularized Coulomb law
$\vect f_t=-\mu\|\vect f_n\|\vect v_t/\sqrt{\|\vect v_t\|^2+\epsilon^2}$.
No clamps, impulses or velocity projections are used.

\subsection{Work Ledger}
The ledger stores $E=T+V_g+V_c$ and the trapezoidal work $W_c$ of every
force category; projections are booked as the energy change they cause.
The certificate and the per-step drift are
\begin{equation}
\varepsilon(t)=E(t)-E_0-\textstyle\sum_c W_c(t),\qquad
\delta_k=\varepsilon_k^{-}-\varepsilon_{k-1},
\end{equation}
where $\varepsilon_k^{-}$ is the residual before the energy row is
applied: $\delta_k$ is the energy that step $k$ created or destroyed
without a booked cause. For a correct model it is discretization error
and shrinks with $\Delta t$; an unbooked force would not. We also report
the numerical work $|W_{\mathrm{num}}|$ of projections and corrector and
the \emph{aid share} of the energy input supplied by non-physical
categories. A run is \emph{admissible} if the aid share is zero and
$\max_k|\delta_k|$ and $|W_{\mathrm{num}}|$ are small compared with the
actuator work.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Sensitivity-Gradient Tipping}\label{sec:sgt}

\subsection{Quasi-Static Sensitivity}
Between tips the rover rests on a support face $\mathcal F$ of three
sticking nodes. Augmenting $\vect q$ with the core ($n'=13$ nodes) and
linearizing the static equilibrium with respect to the rest-length
offsets $\vect u\in\R^{36}$ ($u>0$ shortens) gives
\begin{equation}
\begin{bmatrix}\vect K & \vect A^\top\\ \vect A & \vect 0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}\delta\vect q\\ \delta\vect\mu\end{bmatrix}
=\begin{bmatrix}\vect B\\ \vect 0\end{bmatrix}\delta\vect u,
\quad
\vect A=\begin{bmatrix}\vect R_q\\ \vect E_{\mathcal F}\end{bmatrix},
\label{eq:kkt}
\end{equation}
where $\vect E_{\mathcal F}$ pins the support nodes and $\vect B$
contains $\pm k\vect e$ for every taut cable. $\vect K$ assembles
$k\vect e\vect e^\top+\tfrac tL(\vect I-\vect e\vect e^\top)$ for a
taut cable and the \emph{negative} geometric stiffness
$-\tfrac PL(\vect I-\vect e\vect e^\top)$ for a bar under compression
$P$; axial bar rigidity is a constraint, and a small Tikhonov term keeps
the system regular. One LU factorization gives the displacement
sensitivities $\vect X=\partial\vect q/\partial\vect u$ and the COM
sensitivity $\vect S=\tfrac{1}{m_{\mathrm{tot}}}\sum_i m_i\vect X_i$.

\subsection{Edge Selection and Command}
For an edge $e$ of $\mathcal F$ with outward normal $\vect n_e$ and
midpoint $\vect p_e$, the tipping margin is
$m_e=-(\vect c-\vect p_e)^\top\vect n_e$ and the gradient of the COM
shift across it is $\vect g_e=\vect S_{xy}^\top\vect n_e$. Under box
limits $u_k\in[\underline u_k,\bar u_k]$ the achievable shift is
$s_e=\sum_k\max(g_{e,k}\bar u_k,g_{e,k}\underline u_k)$. Among edges
aligned with the travel direction ($\vect n_e^\top\vect d\ge0.25$), SGT
locks for the cycle the edge with the largest reachable margin
$s_e-m_e$ and commands
\begin{equation}
u_k=\bar u_k\,\mathrm{clip}\big(g_{e,k}/\|\vect g_e\|_\infty,-\rho,1\big),
\label{eq:sgt}
\end{equation}
normalized separately for shell and payload cables. A state machine
(\textsc{Settle}$\to$\textsc{Shift}$\to$\textsc{Tip}$\to$\textsc{Release})
re-plans at 20\,Hz until the support face changes. A support-face
primitive contracts a fixed set whose effect is mostly absorbed by
elastic deformation; the constrained sensitivity instead tells which
cables move the COM, and the compressed bars soften the structure in
exactly the bending directions that tipping needs.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{MPC + GPS: MPC-Guided Policy Search}\label{sec:gps}

\subsection{MPC Teacher}
With $\hat{\vect g}$ the gradient of \eqref{eq:sgt} normalized per
group and $\tilde{\vect u}=\vect u/\bar{\vect u}$, the teacher solves,
over $N$ steps of $\Delta t$,
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\min_{\tilde{\vect u}_{1:N}}\;&\textstyle\sum_{k=1}^{N}\big(-\hat{\vect g}^\top\tilde{\vect u}_k
+\tfrac r2\|\tilde{\vect u}_k\|^2+\tfrac{r_\Delta}{2}\|\tilde{\vect u}_k-\tilde{\vect u}_{k-1}\|^2\big)\\
&+\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|\tilde{\vect u}_1-\pi_\theta(\vect o)\|^2\\
\text{s.t.}\;&\underline{\tilde u}\le\tilde{\vect u}_k\le1,\quad
|\tilde{\vect u}_k-\tilde{\vect u}_{k-1}|\le\rho_s,
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:teacher}
\end{equation}
with $\tilde{\vect u}_0$ the current spool state and $\rho_s$ the spool
speed times $\Delta t$ ($N=6$, $\Delta t=50$\,ms, $r=1$,
$r_\Delta=0.2$). The problem is separable per actuator and is solved by
projected gradient at 20\,Hz.

\remark{1}For $N=1$, $r=1$, $r_\Delta=\lambda=0$ and an inactive rate
bound, each actuator minimizes $-\hat g_k\tilde u_k+\tfrac12\tilde u_k^2$
on $[\underline{\tilde u}_k,1]$, whose solution
$\mathrm{clip}(\hat g_k,\underline{\tilde u}_k,1)$ is the SGT command
\eqref{eq:sgt}. The teacher thus generalizes SGT with a horizon,
spool-rate limits and smoothing, and $\lambda>0$ adds the
policy-proximity term of guided policy search---the quadratic form of
the KL constraint between fixed-covariance Gaussian policies.

\subsection{Policy Observations}
The policy $\pi_\theta$ does not use the KKT model. Each outer cable is
described by 20 local features in the frame of the travel direction:
midpoint relative to the COM, end-node clearances, signed distance to
the locked edge and along it, membership of its end nodes in face and
edge, the sign-invariant orientation terms $(\vect e^\top\vect n_e)e_z$,
$(\vect e^\top\vect n_e)^2$ and $e_z^2$, current offset and strain, and
global context (COM velocity, gait state, margin, time in state); the
payload cables have 19 analogous features. One MLP ($2\times48$ units)
is shared by all outer cables and one ($2\times36$) by all payload
cables, so the policy is equivariant to the cable numbering and
independent of the face the rover rests on.

\subsection{Training}
Starting from $\mathcal D_0$ collected with the unregularized teacher,
iteration $i$ alternates
\begin{subequations}\label{eq:gps}
\begin{align}
&\text{C-step: roll out \eqref{eq:teacher} with }\lambda_i\text{, and }\pi_{\theta_i}\text{ itself,}\\
&\mathcal D_{i+1}=\mathcal D_i\cup\{(\vect o,\tilde{\vect u}^\star_{\lambda=0}(\vect o))\},\\
&\text{S-step: }\theta_{i+1}=\arg\min_\theta\textstyle\sum_{\mathcal D_{i+1}}\|\pi_\theta(\vect o)-\tilde{\vect u}^\star\|^2,
\end{align}
\end{subequations}
i.e.\ every visited state is labelled with the unregularized teacher as
in PLATO \cite{kahn2017plato}, while the executed actions keep the data
close to the learner's own state distribution. We use
$\lambda_i\in\{0.5,1,2,\dots\}$, four 15\,s episodes per iteration (two
of them executing the policy) over Levels 1 and 3 with straight and
$\pm8$--$10$\,m offset goals, and \gpsIterations\ iterations
(\gpsSamples\ labelled actuator samples, Adam).

\subsection{Deployment}
At run time the policy replaces the per-tick KKT solve while the state
machine is kept. Choosing the edge by alignment alone sent the policy to
edges it could not tip over, so the deployed controller solves
\eqref{eq:kkt} once per tip cycle to pick the edge with the largest
reachable margin, as the teacher does, and excludes edges that aborted
from the same face.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Suspension-Integrity Filter}\label{sec:shield}

\subsection{Observation}
Gravity and the outer-cable actuation compress the shell while it rolls:
under SGT the mean node height drops from \sagInitialHeight\ to
\sagMeanHeight\,m (\sagPercent\,\%). The node-to-payload distances
shrink with it, and the payload cables, pretensioned to
\sagDesignTension\,N, carry \sagMeanTension\,N on average; at least one
of the 12 is slack in \shAnySlackOff\,\% of the samples
(Fig.~\ref{fig:teaser}e). The ``suspended'' payload is loose in the cage
for most of the motion.

\subsection{Filter}
Given the command $\vect u_{\mathrm{nom}}$ of any tipping controller,
the filter returns
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\vect u^\star=\arg\min_{\vect u}\;&\tfrac12(\vect u-\vect u_{\mathrm{nom}})^\top\vect W(\vect u-\vect u_{\mathrm{nom}})\\
\text{s.t.}\;&\hat h_c(\vect u)\ge(1-\gamma)\,h_c,\quad c\in\mathcal C,\\
&\hat{\vect g}^\top(\vect u-\vect u_0)\ge\hat{\vect g}^\top(\vect u_{\mathrm{nom}}-\vect u_0),\quad
\underline{\vect u}\le\vect u\le\bar{\vect u},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:shield}
\end{equation}
where $\vect u_0$ is the current command and $\hat h_c$ is the
first-order prediction of a safety function from $\vect X$. For a cable
between nodes $i,j$ with stiffness $k$, rest length $l_0$ and direction
$\vect e$,
$\hat T(\vect u)=k\big(L-l_0+u_{\mathrm{self}}+\vect e^\top(\vect X_j-\vect X_i)(\vect u-\vect u_0)\big)$.
$\mathcal C$ contains payload-cable tension $T\ge10$\,N, outer-cable
tension $T\le150$\,N and payload-to-rod clearance $d\ge0.08$\,m (core
radius 0.05\,m), the latter linearized at the closest point of each rod.
The barrier condition is the discrete-time form of
\cite{agrawal2017dcbf}: a satisfied constraint stays satisfied and a
violated one recovers at rate $\gamma=0.3$ per step. The second
constraint preserves the predicted COM shift: without it the filter
cancels the payload-cable slackening that SGT uses to tip; with it the
tipping effort is re-routed, mainly to the leading payload cables. It
is dropped if it conflicts with the barriers. $\vect W$ weights outer
cables ten times more than payload cables, and the QP is solved by
accelerated projected gradient on the dual \cite{beck2009fista} with the
box exact in the primal.

\remark{2}The conditions hold for the quasi-static prediction $\hat h$.
Tumbling and impacts are inertial events that this prediction does not
contain, so the closed-loop results of Section~\ref{sec:res-shield} are
empirical, and we report where they fail.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Results}\label{sec:results}

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\emph{Platform.} Shell radius 0.5\,m (bar length 0.851\,m), 12 nodes of
0.2\,kg, six bars of 0.3\,kg, payload 1.6\,kg (5.8\,kg in total), cable
stiffness 1200\,N/m (payload cables 1600\,N/m). Every method uses the
same actuator box: stroke 0.15\,m (30\,\% of the 0.49\,m rest length)
and 0.20\,m/s spool speed. Physics runs at 500\,Hz, controllers at
20\,Hz, on the DAE core with \eqref{eq:corr}, passive contact and zero
aids, on terrain Level~1 for 20\,s unless stated otherwise.

\emph{Baselines.} \emph{Support-face heuristic}: the fixed contraction
primitive. \emph{LQR, iLQR, QP-MPC}: the controllers of the original
code base, which solve a two-state reduced-order rolling model for a
normalized effort that scales the same primitive. \emph{Legacy+assist}$^\dagger$:
the original penalty+SHAKE engine with roll couple, traction, grip and
corridor aids, reported as an inadmissible reference.

\emph{Scenarios and metrics.} Lateral impulse 0.5\,m/s at 6\,s; push
10\,N for 2\,s; Gaussian, Laplace and outlier (2\,\%, $10\times$)
sensor noise; cable stiffness $-20\,\%$, friction $-40\,\%$, payload
$+30\,\%$; actuation delay 100\,ms. We report mean speed $\bar v$,
cross-track error $e(t)=x_c(t)-x_c(0)$ (RMS and max), success
($\Delta y\ge1$\,m in 20\,s), effort $\int\vect u^\top\vect u\,dt$, cost of
transport $\mathrm{CoT}=W_{\mathrm{act}}/(mg\Delta y)$, controller time
and the ledger quantities of Section~\ref{sec:model}; statistics are
mean\,$\pm$\,std over seeds 1--5 (nominal) or 1--3. The policy is
evaluated on \gpsEvalConditions\ held-out conditions (unseen seeds,
Levels 1 and 3, straight and $\pm6$\,m goals); the filter on
\shConditions\ paired conditions (three seeds on Level~1, two on
Level~3, push, impulse, payload $+30\,\%$, delay, stiffness $-20\,\%$)
with payload-cable slack time and tension, payload rattle (RMS position
relative to the shell centroid), 99th-percentile payload acceleration,
minimal payload--rod clearance and maximal outer-cable tension, measured
after the first second.

\subsection{MPC + GPS}
\input{../results/paper/tables/gps.tex}
On the held-out conditions the learned policy advances
\gpsPolicyProgress\,m in 20\,s, \gpsRatio\,\% of SGT
(\gpsSgtProgress\,m) and \gpsTeacherRatio\,\% of the teacher
(\gpsTeacherProgress\,m), with \gpsPolicyAborts\ aborted cycles per run
(Table~\ref{tab:gps}), and exceeds SGT in one condition
(\gpsBestPolicy\ vs.\ \gpsBestSgt\,m). The unregularized teacher is
itself slightly faster than SGT, which we attribute to its rate-aware
smoothing. The policy is not cheaper per tick in our implementation
(\gpsPolicyMs\ vs.\ \gpsSgtMs\,ms): for 13 nodes the KKT solve is
already inexpensive, so the value of the policy lies in replacing the
model evaluation by a learned map, not in speed.

\subsection{Suspension Integrity}\label{sec:res-shield}
\input{../results/paper/tables/shield.tex}
With the filter the payload cables are slack \shSlackOnSgt\,\% of the
time under SGT (\shSlackOffSgt\,\% without) and \shSlackOnGps\,\% under
the policy (\shSlackOffGps\,\%), in all \shConditions\ conditions
(Table~\ref{tab:shield}); the mean payload-cable tension rises from
\shTensionOffSgt\ to \shTensionOnSgt\,N (Fig.~\ref{fig:teaser}e). For
SGT the taut suspension also makes tipping more effective: progress
increases from \shProgOffSgt\ to \shProgOnSgt\,m ($+\shProgGainSgt\,\%$,
better in \shProgBetterSgt\ of \shConditions\ conditions) and aborted
cycles fall from \shAbortOffSgt\ to \shAbortOnSgt. For the policy the
filter restores the suspension at unchanged progress (\shProgOffGps\ vs.\
\shProgOnGps\,m). It does not reduce peak loads: in \shClearViol\ of
\shFilteredRuns\ filtered runs the payload came closer than 0.08\,m to
a rod (minimum \shClearMin\,m), in \shOuterViol\ runs an outer cable
exceeded 150\,N, and the 99th-percentile payload acceleration of SGT
increased---the inertial events excluded by Remark~2. The filter adds
\shMs\,ms per control step.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Conclusion and Future Perspectives}
We made tensegrity-rover simulation auditable with a non-minimal
Lagrangian DAE, a minimum-norm constraint-and-energy corrector, passive
contact with a potential and a work ledger that measures the unexplained
energy of every step before it is corrected; it exposes the
kilojoule-scale projection exchange and the non-physical aids of a
conventional engine. On this basis, sensitivity-gradient tipping rolls
a six-bar rover with a heavy payload using cables only, where
reduced-order schedulers of a fixed primitive do not. The same
sensitivity model serves as the teacher of MPC-guided policy search,
whose per-cable policy reaches \gpsRatio\,\% of SGT's progress, and as
the prediction model of a suspension-integrity filter that keeps the
payload cables taut and makes SGT \shProgGainSgt\,\% faster.

\emph{Limitations.} All results are in simulation with contact and cable
parameters not identified on hardware; the ledger bounds the energy
contributed by integrator, projections and aids but does not validate
the model against reality. SGT is quasi-static, re-plans at 20\,Hz
(about \SI{0.1}{m/s}), is sensitive to heavy-tailed measurement noise
and zig-zags because its edge choice is greedy per cycle. The policy
imitates a teacher on the same model, needs one KKT solve per cycle and
is not faster than SGT; the filter guarantees nothing during impacts.

\remark{3}The modelled shell is a regular icosahedron ($d/h=1/\varphi$).
A form-finding analysis with the TsgFEM equilibrium matrix
\cite{ma2022tsgfem} shows that this shape admits no self-stress state,
whereas the expanded octahedron ($d/h=0.5$) admits one; the modelled
rest geometry is therefore not a prestressed equilibrium, and part of
the observed sag may originate there.

\emph{Future perspectives.} A second-order barrier on the DAE dynamics
for impact-safe payload clearance; repeating the studies on the
form-found shape; a robust estimator in front of the planner and a
heading-aware edge selection; and hardware validation.

\texttt{npm run experiments \&\& npm run paper:data \&\& npm run paper:ext}
reruns all experiments and regenerates every table, figure and number
(\coderepo).
